title: Adjournment Motion on Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary school students
what_it_is: An Adjournment Motion speech by Mr David Hoe proposing Curiosity Credits 2.0 for secondary school students, followed by a response from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi, before Parliament adjourned.
why_it_matters: The record does not set out the practical impact.

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe proposed Curiosity Credits 2.0 to help secondary school students make more informed post-secondary school choices.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: today, I want to build on this idea and focus on Curiosity Credits 2.0 – helping secondary school students to make more informed post-secondary school choices.

key_points.point: He asked whether MOE can study and pilot a more structured way to help students who learn best through experience.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: I would, therefore, like to ask whether MOE can study and pilot a more structured way to help students who learn best through experience.

key_points.point: Under the proposal, from Secondary 1 onwards students would have a Curiosity Credits wallet.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: From Secondary 1 onwards, students would have this thing that I call a Curiosity Credits wallet.

key_points.point: The taster sessions would be designed by ITEs, polytechnics, universities or specialised institutions, and schools could bring them into classrooms or students could attend them at institutions during protected exposure periods.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: These taster sessions are designed by ITEs, polytechnics, universities or specialised institutions, and schools can bring these tasters into the school and into the classrooms during selected weeks and also allow students to attend them at these institutions during protected exposure periods.

key_points.point: He said the aim is structured exposure, not an open-ended voucher scheme.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: The aim here is not to create an open-ended voucher scheme. The aim is to provide structured exposure.

key_points.point: He set a target that by Secondary 4 students could have about six to eight structured taster experiences in different clusters.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: if by Secondary 4, they can have about six to eight structured taster experiences in different clusters, this might help them to make a better decision.

key_points.point: He proposed safeguards including that it should not be cash but credits and entitlement used for approved programmes.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: First, it should not be cash. It should be credits and entitlement used for approved programmes.

key_points.point: He said the issue is fit, not whether junior college, polytechnic or ITE is better.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: The issue is not whether junior college, polytechnic or ITE is better. The issue is fit.

key_points.point: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi said MOE is open to ideas like Mr Hoe's that can bolster existing programmes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Experience is indeed a great teacher and we are open to ideas, like Mr Hoe's, that can bolster our existing range of programmes to guide our students in their educational journeys.

key_points.point: He offered a different perspective on the aspect of the Motion that not having the perfect fit at 16 means it could be too late.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: But I would also like to gently offer a different perspective on one aspect of Mr Hoe's Motion – that is not having the perfect fit at 16 means it could be too late.

key_points.point: He said MOE has a three-pronged approach to supporting students to discover interests and strengths, develop potential and choose post-secondary pathways.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: With this goal in mind, MOE has a three-pronged approach in supporting students to discover their interests and strengths, develop their potential and choose their post-secondary pathways wisely.

key_points.point: He said polytechnics and ITE offer three-day Applied Learning Modules.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: polytechnics and ITE offer three-day Applied Learning Modules (ApLMs)

key_points.point: He said MOE's Opportunity Fund provides financial support for disadvantaged students to access development opportunities.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: MOE's Opportunity Fund also provides financial support to enable such students to access development opportunities.

key_points.point: He said Pathfinder Plus has Secondary 3 and 4 students from disadvantaged backgrounds attend workshops curated according to their strengths.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Through MOE's Pathfinder Plus programme, Secondary 3 and 4 students from disadvantaged backgrounds attend workshops that MOE curates according to the students' strengths.

key_points.point: He said under MSF's ComLink+ programme, SSO family coaches and FSC case workers work with lower-income families with children below 21.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Under MSF's ComLink+ programme, dedicated SSO family coaches and FSC case workers work with lower-income families with children below 21, to support the child's education while helping the family address broader challenges that may affect their progress towards their long-term goals.

key_points.point: He said finding the right post-secondary path does not have to happen all at once or perfectly on the first try.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Let me come back to something I said earlier, that finding the right post-secondary path does not have to happen all at once, or perfectly, on the first try.

key_points.point: He gave the example of Tan Hock Yang, who initially wanted Aerospace Engineering but later took a Diploma in Supply Chain Management.
key_points.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
key_points.quote: Hock Yang initially wanted to follow in his brother's footsteps into Aerospace Engineering, but soon realised that it was not his cup of tea while pursuing a diploma in that field.

what_happens_next: Adjourned accordingly at 8.24 pm; the transcript does not state a next step for the Curiosity Credits 2.0 proposal.
not_said: Will MOE study or pilot Curiosity Credits 2.0?
How would a Curiosity Credits wallet be funded and administered?
Which students would be eligible for Curiosity Credits and how many credits would each receive?
How would taster sessions be scheduled within protected curriculum time?
How would the outcomes of any pilot be evaluated?
Would existing Applied Learning Modules be expanded or changed?
How would the proposal interact with existing programmes such as the Opportunity Fund, Pathfinder Plus and ComLink+?
What support is available for students who have already chosen a poor-fit post-secondary pathway?
Would guidance practices for 16-year-olds considering junior college change?
